what: Archival catalogue descriptions of Tolkien material, from two repositories' own catalogues: 355 from The National Archives Discovery (covering six holding repositories, chiefly Reading and the Tolkien Society Archives) and 983 from Marquette University's own finding aid. CATALOGUE METADATA ONLY -- shelfmark, title, date, extent, language, form. No manuscript text and no image of any manuscript is reproduced or served.
no_tier: THESE ROWS CARRY NO TIER, DELIBERATELY. The tier hierarchy ranks CLAIMS ABOUT ARDA by their distance from Tolkien's own word. A row saying that Reading holds a file of letters, one folder, in English is a claim about READING, not about Middle-earth, and a tier on it would assert something the record does not say. Every row carries a HAND -- who wrote the description -- and a LICENCE, which are the properties a catalogue record actually has. On the fifth tier see his ruling C474: tier 5 is an ORIGIN axis, 'made by this archive', and the Arda rank lives beside it as content_tier; nothing here carries either.

catalogues.title: The National Archives Discovery catalogue
catalogues.why_one_request: AN EARLIER 4-PAGE x 100 WALK REPORTED 335 DISTINCT RECORDS FROM 355 ROWS: 20 ids came back twice, because Discovery's relevance sort is not stable across page boundaries. One request with resultsPageSize=1000 returns 355 distinct records, and this generator refuses on a duplicate id rather than trusting that.
catalogues.why_per_record_details: The search endpoint returns neither extent nor language. Both were obtained by calling /records/v1/details/{id} once per record: 311 of 355 carry an extent, 317 a language.
catalogues.url_note: The API URL on each row is the surface the record was retrieved from and the one a machine can re-fetch. The human-facing permalink at discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/{id} was MEASURED on 2026-08-26 to return HTTP 202 with a 2,019-byte AWS WAF JavaScript challenge, not the record; it is a browser-only URL and is carried beside the API URL, not instead of it.
catalogues.extent_note: Discovery exposes a single field, physicalDescriptionForm, which mixes extent and form ("1 folder (2 items)", "1 file"). It is recorded verbatim under `extent`; `form` is absent from these rows because the source does not separate them.
catalogues.stale_if: TNA re-indexes; the Tolkien free-text result count (355 on 2026-08-26) changes; contributing repositories revise their deposits.
catalogues.access_falsifier: A later GET of the row's API URL returning a non-200, or a body that does not parse as JSON with `id` equal to the row's record_id, falsifies its `access_status: live`. Every body was sniffed and the id matched at capture time.

catalogues.title: Marquette University, J.R.R. Tolkien Collection and allied collections, published finding aid
catalogues.notation: SERIES / BOX / FOLDER THROUGHOUT. The string "MSS-JRRT" in these shelfmarks is the COLLECTION code, not an installment number. The other notation Marquette uses, `MSS-N/B/F`, is the Nth installment of LORD OF THE RINGS ADDITIONAL MANUSCRIPTS PRESENTED BY CHRISTOPHER TOLKIEN, and IT IS NOT THE SAME SPACE: MSS-3/1/9 is the Third Installment, not main Series 3. No installment record is in this dataset; site/arda_witnesses.json holds those 236.
catalogues.extent_note: Marquette records extent in the finding aid as leaves/pages ("5/8"); parsed verbatim, unit not restated by the source.
catalogues.stale_if: Marquette revises the finding aid; accessions from the Tolkien Estate are added.
catalogues.access_falsifier: A later GET of the row's URL whose body sha256 differs from the row's content_hash_page_sha256 means the finding aid changed; a non-200, or a body with no <table> carrying Box/Folder headers, falsifies its `access_status: live`.

tna_ogl_v3_scope_unverified.as_stated: "All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated" -- footer of https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/terms-and-conditions/, retrieved 2026-08-26.
tna_ogl_v3_scope_unverified.the_open_question: IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THIS REACHES THE CONTRIBUTED CATALOGUE DESCRIPTIONS, which are most of this set. A description whose Discovery `source` is A2A, NRA or Archon was authored by the holding repository, not by TNA, and nothing on the terms page says TNA's footer licenses another body's text. Recorded as an open question rather than resolved in the archive's own favour.
tna_ogl_v3_scope_unverified.crawl_conditions_as_stated: https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/terms-and-conditions/policy-on-use-of-website-and-catalogue-data/ : "If you are not using a browser, you must identify yourself, your web scraper or crawler with a legitimate user agent string... We do not accept anonymous user agents". Rate limit 3,000 requests / 5 minutes.
tna_ogl_v3_scope_unverified.basis: Read from the stated terms pages, not inferred from reputation.

marquette_no_open_licence.as_stated: No open licence is stated. https://www.marquette.edu/library/archives/using-images.php states that written permission of the Raynor Library must be obtained to use any item or quotation beyond fair use, and requires the credit line "Marquette University, Department of Archival Collections and Institutional Repository". Site footer states "© 2026 Marquette University".
marquette_no_open_licence.what_is_carried_here: Catalogue metadata only -- shelfmark, folder title, stated extent and form, as the finding aid publishes them. No manuscript text and no image is reproduced by this archive, and the mandated credit line is on every row.
marquette_no_open_licence.basis: Read from the Marquette rights page and page footer as retrieved 2026-08-26; NOT inferred.

hand_basis.contributed_to_discovery: The description was contributed to TNA Discovery by the holding repository (Discovery `source` A2A, NRA or Archon). The HAND is that repository, and it is the reason the OGL question above is open rather than settled.
hand_basis.discovery_source_unmapped: TNA Discovery returns a `source` code this harvest did not map to an authoring body. WHO WROTE THIS DESCRIPTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is left unestablished rather than assigned to TNA because TNA's footer would then license it.
hand_basis.repository_finding_aid: The description is the repository's own published finding aid, written by the repository.

recovered_descriptions.what: MARQUETTE PUBLISHES THE FOLDER DESCRIPTION UNDER THREE DIFFERENT COLUMN HEADINGS AND THE STAGED HARVEST READ ONE OF THEM. Its build step took `contents` only, so 482 of its 983 rows arrived carrying a shelfmark and nothing else. The text was in its own capture all along -- the stage's inventory file, same page sha256, same retrieved_at -- and is read from there, row by row, with the alignment checked on every run. Every row records the heading its description came from in `title_column`, so this repair is checkable and reversible. Nothing was re-fetched.

relation_to_witnesses.what: THIS IS NOT A SECOND REGISTER OF THE SAME THING. arda_witnesses.json holds the folders THE CORPUS CITES, and the value it owns is the resolved corpus links its generator proved by subject agreement. This dataset holds a catalogue harvest with NO corpus join. Where both describe the same folder, the row here names the sibling's shelfmark in `also_in_witnesses` so the duplication is visible and joinable instead of silent.
relation_to_witnesses.held_only_by_witnesses: the 236 MSS-N/B/F installment records, which this harvest does not cover
relation_to_witnesses.why_not_merged: The two are independent parses of one repository's pages and they carry different fields; merging them needs a join on folder identity that has not been demonstrated, and one sampled corpus citation (mss4box11folder18) already fails to resolve against the published Series 4 inventory. The overlap is DECLARED, not resolved.

refused.what: A join from Marquette's finding aid to the corpus's own citation strings.
refused.why: One sampled citation, `mss4box11folder18`, does not resolve against the published Series 4 inventory, which runs to Box 1 and an Oversize box. A mapping that fails on its sampled case is not a mapping. These rows land as WHAT MARQUETTE PUBLISHES; the corpus join stays where it has been demonstrated, in site/arda_witnesses.json.

refused.what: Extending TNA's Open Government Licence to the contributed descriptions.
refused.why: 330 of 355 TNA rows come from A2A, NRA or another contributed source, authored by the holding repository. TNA's footer licenses TNA's content; nothing read says it licenses another body's text. Recorded as an open question on every affected row.
The hierarchy ranks claims about Arda and a catalogue record makes none. See `no_tier`.

rows.description: This fonds comprises the administrative records of the Tolkien Society, from its foundation in 1969 to the present day (2003). These include minutes of Committee meetings and AGMs, accounts and other financial papers, and material relating to the Society's publications, Oxonmoot, the 1992 Centenary Conference, and Tolkien Society Trading Ltd. A series of Subject Files, comprises correspondence and papers relating to subjects of interest, including copyright and trademarking, publishers, the Archive and Lending Library, the Tolkien Society Working Party, and workshops and seminars for example. The fonds also contains a large amount of correspondence, in the Chairman's papers and the Publicity Officer's papers series'. Papers relating to the educational outreach activities of the Society have not yet been transferred to the Archive.

rows.description: Papers relating to the Society's aim, as set out in its Constitution, to establish a memorial centre devoted to study, exhibitions and lectures relating to the life and works of J.R.R. Tolkien, preferably in a location associated with him. The file comprises the agenda and minutes of the Tolkien Memorial Centre Committee, established to realise this aim, 25 July 1992-27 January 1993. It also includes correspondence between Committee members with related papers, May 1992-July 1996, including a draft Tolkien Memorial Centre Leaflet; a newspaper clipping from the Evening Echo, Bournemouth, 1 April 1993, regarding the likely choice of Bournemouth as the location of the Centre; an announcement entitled 'Tolkien Centre Status at July 1996', summarising the minutes of the Committee meetings, and any decisions made.

rows.description: This list consists of eight sub fonds relating to different types of material collected by the Society. The Society actively collects all kinds of material relating to Tokien's life and work, including books (subfonds TSB); artworks inspired by Tolkien, such as paintings, drawings and sculpture (subfonds TSCR); ephemeral items, including posters and general advertising material (subfonds TSE); journals (subfinds TSJ); recordings using a variety of media, (subfonds TSM); newspaper clippings (subfonds TSN); and photographs (subfonds TSPH). Subfonds TSP consists of the administrative papers of the Society itself, including minutes, correspondence and accounts. : . : :

rows.title: Tolkien Society Ephemera Collection
rows.description: The Tolkien Society collects material of an ephemeral nature relating to Tolkien and his works, events including plays and performances, and to fandom in general. The Collection includes posters, calendars, diaries, advertising material and any other items, produced commercially and by individual fans, or other Tolkien Societies, and also typescripts and manuscripts of unpublished works of Tolkien criticism, and photocopies of items from publications not in the Books or Journal Collections [Ref: TSB and TSJ]. Other items of note in the Collection include: memorabilia relating to Sarehole Mill and the Eagle and Child, Oxford; information on various smials; copies of some of J.R.R. Tolkien's letters, and his will; transcripts of interviews he gave; a list of the contents of his own library; a bibliography of books about him; a pronounciation guide to words found in the Lord of the Rings; a copy of the contents of the Tolkien Collection at Marquette University, Wisconsin; and extracts from catalogues where some of Tolkien's letters, and other items, were put up for auction The collection is not fully catalogued
rows.hand: Tolkien Society Archives

rows.description: Email correspondence between Committee members regarding the possible establishment of an 'official' Lord of the Rings Fan Club by Fantastic Media following the release of the film trilogy by Peter Jackson. Discussion centres on how the Tolkien Society should respond to this claim, in their position as the only club/society endorsed by the Professor himself, and how they could publicise their existence in the midst of a possible proliferation of further fan clubs. Includes a letter from Manches, the solicitors to the Tolkien Estate, stating that Fantastic Media's proposal had been blocked for legal reasons.

rows.description: These journals include scholarly works based on Tolkien's writings, other fantasy fiction and philology, and commercial publications, collected because they concern the film adaptations of the Lord of the Rings, or they relate to some aspect of Tolkien's life and works, or similar works. The larger part of the Collection comprises fanzines and journals produced by Tolkien fans and similar societies worldwide, many of which had a limited readership, and have since been discontinued. The Collection also includes microfilms of Tolkien-themed journal collections held by other individuals and institutions [not included in this cataloguing project].

rows.repository: Tolkien Society Archives

rows.title: Tolkien Society Books Collection
rows.description: The Tolkien Society collects editions of the works of J.R.R. Tolkien and related works, in their original languages and in translation The collection includes copies of most English language editions of 'The Hobbit' and 'The Lord of the Rings', at least one edition of virtually every other published work by Tolkien, and editions in translation in almost every European language, including Aragonese, Croatian, Latvian and Faeroese, and in Hebrew, Indonesian, Japanese and Esperanto. There are also photocopies in the Ephemera Collection [Ref: TSE] of editions which are not held in this Collection. Also in the collection are biographies of Tolkien and studies of the 'Inklings', the group of Oxford-based writers which included Tolkien and C.S. Lewis; editions of Tolkien's letters; critical and analytical works on the subjects of the mythology, language and art of his works; and reminiscences and analyses by members of his family There are a few works which relate to Tolkien's background, such as a history of the Catholic Church in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, and a family Bible; and the Society has acquired an edition of C.S. Lewis's 'Chronicles of Narnia', written by a fellow 'Inkling', and 'Beowulf', as an example of works which are said to have inspired Tolkien. Books inspired by his work include guides to and atlases of Middle Earth; Tolkien and Hobbit 'Companions'; comic books; books about the films of the 'The Lord of the Rings'; and parodies.

rows.title: Tolkien Society Creative Responses Collection
rows.description: The Tolkien Society collects material produced in 'creative response' to Tolkien's works. Original artwork by persons inspired by the author's writings, 1970-2003, often depicting characters and scenes in Tolkien's literature. Many of these works were submitted for publication in one of the Society's journals. The Collection includes drawings produced by children at events held at Sarehole Mill, Birmingham, and the original artwork for Barbera Strachey's 'Journeys of Frodo'. Objects, 1967-2003, again produced by persons inspired by Tolkien's works, as well as items commercially produced, for the consumption of fandom. Objects produced by fans include an empty bottle of 'Northfarthing' beer, a beer mug, and banners. Commercially produced items include a complete set of 'Myth and Magic' figurines, games, and a growing collection of food packaging relating to the Peter Jackson films, and sales items produced by the Tolkien Society, and its subsidiary, Tolkien Society Trading Ltd, such as a tie produced for the 1992 Tolkien Centenary Conference, and sweatshirts, inlcuding one with an original design by Pauline Baynes. Publicity and sales literature for many commercIal objects can be found in the Society's Ephemera Collection [Ref: TSE]. The collection is not catalogued

rows.hand: Tolkien Society Archives

The letters are mainly to and from the editors, Patricia Reynolds and Glen Goodknight, although letters from printers and typesetters, and those who gave papers at the Conference are also present.

The file also includes letters to and from members of the Mythopoeic Society.
rows.hand: Tolkien Society Archives

rows.repository: Tolkien Society Archives
rows.collection: Tolkien Society Archive.Tolkien Society Papers.1992 Tolkien Centenary Conference.
rows.title: Miscellaneous 1992 papers
rows.description: This file comprises various documents relating to the 1992 Centenary Conference. It includes printer ready copies of various Conference posters, information sheets, timetables, Progress Reports 3-6 and Supplements, the Souvenir Guide, the text for the Tolkien travelling exhibition with a list of venues hosting it, and the Conference headed notepaper incorporating the Mythopoeic Society's logo. Other items include a bibliography of Christopher Tolkien, various press releases, a plan of the seating arrangement for the Banquet, an explanation of how the voodoo board was to work, a list of persons who did not attend, various short essays including one on the history of the Mythopoeic Society, and a second on Tolkien's association with Oxford Colleges, and a Tolkien Family Tree.
rows.hand: Tolkien Society Archives

rows.repository: Hackney Archives
rows.collection: Small Collections.
rows.title: DEEDS & CORRESPONDENCE
rows.description: Concerning the will of Daniel Tolkien, furrier (d.1813) and provisions made concerning his widow Ann, who had the house in Hoxton Town and monies from leasehold property Nos 7-9 inc Cumberland Street, Hackney Road [later Scawfell Street]. One of Tolkein's daughters, Maria, married David Wotherspoon, who died before 1823, at which time she married Edwin Cuthbert. A settlement was drawn up at this time, which Cuthbert later defaulted on and was imprisoned in the Marshelsea for debt in the same year. The documents include Tolkein's will, correspondence and receipts and a bond in which David Wotherspoon was involved in 1820 concerning rate collection in Clapham.
rows.hand: Hackney Archives

rows.collection: Records of George Allen & Unwin Ltd.Correspondence files.Correspondence files, boxes 771-780.
rows.title: Letters between George Allen & Unwin Ltd and correspondents whose names begin TI-TOQ
rows.description: Includes correspondence with: Tokyo Institute for Municipal Research who publish a translation into Japanese of Great cities of the world edited by William A. Robson; Tom Todd of Todd Publishing who, through illness, is unable to partner Stanley Unwin in the publishers' team for their tennis match against W.H. Smith & Son which, in consequence, is lost five matches to four; the author in preparations to publish Courtship of animals by Nikko Tinberg. Also includes a letter from Rayner Unwin to J.R.R. Tolkien informing him that he has won the International Fantasy Award for 1956/7 and is due to be presented with 'a 2 foot high chromium rocket incorporating a Ronson lighter'.

rows.repository: University of Reading: Special Collections
rows.collection: Records of Jonathan Cape Ltd.Book files.Book files for books published in 1974.
rows.title: Correspondence relating to the publication of The Times anthology of children's stories illustrated by Pat Marriott
rows.description: Book published as: The Times anthology of children's stories / illustrated by Pat Marriott (London: Jonathan Cape, 1974) ISBN 0224010026 Contents: editorial correspondence file. Includes: 1 letter from illustrator Pat Marriott; 1 letter (copy) from J.R.R. Tolkien declining an invitation to judge a children's story competition; numerous letters from correspondents entering the Sunday Times Prizewinning Children's Story competition; ts of article to introduce the competition by Paul Jennings; letters from The Times regarding copyright; letters and a postcard from Joan Aiken and Valerie Singleton (and The Bagenal Harvey Organisation on her behalf), judges of the competition; 1 letter from Biddy Baxter; letters from prizewinner Ken Whitmore regarding writing projects, reviews for the anthology and a radio play; ts of radio play 'Jump' by Whitmore (36p.); various correspondence regarding reviews for the anthology; letters from prizewinner Ted Allan including letters about his book 'Willie the Squowse' (with letter from Canadian publishers McClelland and Stewart to Allan); 1 letter from prizewinner Helen Day; letters from D.M. Day, father of Helen Day; 1 letter from prizewinner Catherine Ogden; letters from Mrs B (Josephine) Lee; letters from literary agents Bolt & Watson regarding 'Willie the Squowse'; letters from Leo Rost regarding film/television rights to 'The Squouse'; letters from various contributors to the anthology; ts of competition entry 'It's always you who starts the arguments' by Tanya Jo Wesker; letters from Frances Gapper; ts competition shortlist; publicity note; corrected publisher's note. Accompanied by the production file which contains specimen pages and production correspondence and estimates. Holographs, typescripts, photocopies and carbon typescripts. From the Cape book files - 1974 Tim - Wat
rows.access_conditions_as_stated: Prior permission from Random House is required. Please contact University of Reading, Special Collections for further information.
